findings.title: Two of #927's own commits land the production change before the matching test retarget, leaving pre-existing tests broken at the intermediate commit -- verified by checkout, and undisclosed in the ticket's own report
findings.evidence: Commit order (oldest first): 5a3238bde 'feat(db): #927 close propose/sign/run_adjustment_manual ...' THEN 1a824cae7 'test(db): #927 retarget the eight x42-adj batteries ...'; and 8ce2ff304 'feat(web): #927 retire the Propose/Sign/Run-now controls ...' THEN 4a1755b62 'test(web): #927 update the adjustments lane's unit tests ...'. Checking out 8ce2ff304 alone and running apps/web/lib/registers/adjustments.test.ts produces a hard module-load SyntaxError ('does not provide an export named proposeAdjustmentTemplate'), and adjustments-keyboard.test.tsx fails an assertion expecting a 'Propose template' button that commit already removed. Checking out 5a3238bde alone and running packages/db/tests/x42-adjustments.test.mjs against the (shared, already-migrated) clara_l05 fails 12/12, each on the new CLR10 refusal the un-retargeted assertions do not expect. Both were independently reproduced this session (see verification_performed) and the worktree was restored cleanly afterward.
findings.required_fix: No code fix needed at HEAD -- the final state is fully green and independently re-verified (10/10 db, 20/20 web). Flagged because WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 explicitly asks for 'commit per green slice or per small group of slices' and rule 1 assumes every landed commit is a safe resume/bisect point ('never redo landed commits; continue from them'); this pair of splits breaks that assumption for two different subsystems of the SAME ticket. The sibling tickets in this very lane hit the identical structural tension (a retirement's production edit cannot be split into a smaller red-green step) and handled it correctly: #928's report carries an explicit '## Vacuity control (work-order rule 4)' section documenting that the production edit landed first and the red-then-green proof was instead done by hand (git stash revert, re-run, observe red, restore); #929's report has the identical section for its own migration. #927's report contains no equivalent disclosure or justification for either its db-side or web-side split, and its Gates section reports the whole ticket clean without noting that two of its own commits, taken alone, do not pass the tests that existed before the ticket started. The fix, for the next ticket that needs this shape, is either (a) bundle the production edit and its matching test retarget into ONE commit per subsystem (still 'a small group of slices'), or (b) keep them split but add the same '## Vacuity control' disclosure #928/#929 used.

summary: Migration house law (header, prestate sha256(prosrc) pins measured live on clara_l05, the change, tail assertions with a real behavioural call-and-catch proof rather than prosrc inspection alone, a preintegration-gate module with a stable stem, the gate-chain entry in migration order, owner/SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/ACL preservation on every recut body, no new relation so FORCE RLS is not applicable, no rig-meta cohort where none is owed) is fully and correctly followed across all four migrations (0280-0283), and every load-bearing claim spot-checked this session -- live sha256(prosrc) re-derivation, a real door call reproducing the CLR10 refusal, the frozen-workflow and parts-parity checks, the ARCHITECTURE.md:498-502 quote, the CONTEXT.md in-place edits, the gate-chain ordering, and the final green test counts for both the db and web batteries -- reproduced exactly as the ticket reports claim. No PRD/ARCHITECTURE edit, no applied migration edited (0280/0281 each touched by exactly one commit, their own), no frozen-manifest diff. The one real finding (F1, major) is a commit-hygiene violation specific to ticket #927: two of its own commits (one db, one web) land the production change before the matching test retarget, independently verified by checkout to leave pre-existing tests broken (including a hard module-load SyntaxError on the web side) at that intermediate commit -- a real breach of WORK-ORDER.md rule 4's 'commit per green slice' -- and, unlike the identical structural tension #928 and #929 hit and explicitly disclosed under their own '## Vacuity control' headings, #927's report does not disclose or justify it. Final HEAD is fully green and correct; this is a process/transparency finding about the commit sequence, not a defect in the shipped behaviour. Two note-level, no-fix-owed observations (F2, F3) are recorded for completeness.
